title: HA stop mid-solve raises a persistent solve_worker_fallback repair that no later solve ever clears
claim: When EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP fires while a solve's reply is being read from the process worker, the reap breaks the pipe, _await_optimize takes the fallback route (one in-process GIL solve during the stop) and raises the persistent 'solve_worker_fallback' repair; after a restart the issue is still raised once the new instance has solved twice through a healthy worker (count 1, null control 0).
mechanism: _shutdown_process_pool kills the child before taking the lock (by design, D1-s2-05), so the in-flight _run_in_process reads EOF and raises ProcessWorkerUnavailable('Ran out of input'); _await_optimize treats that like a broken install: _note_worker_fallback creates the issue with is_persistent=True and reruns the solve in process. The issue is cleared only by _clear_worker_fallback, which returns early unless THIS process's _WORKER_FALLBACK_CAUSES latched a cause for the entry; after the restart the module dict is empty, so every successful solve leaves the restored issue in place. HA does not unload entries at stop, so _release_registrations' clear does not run either.

evidence.machine: box B4 container, linux x86_64, Python 3.14 venv-ci
evidence.contention_note: part B of m4_race.py and other finder seats running on the box; a count, contention-immune; thread_factor is the residual after subtracting executor-thread CPU (rl.DELIBERATE)

instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:_clear_worker_fallback (with _await_optimize, _note_worker_fallback, async_register_worker_shutdown._stop driven on a real loop)

perturbation.change: _clear_worker_fallback deletes the issue whenever no cause is latched in this process (drop the early return after the pop); harness flag --perturb

metric_definition: Count of hass.issues entries with issue_id solve_worker_fallback after the restarted instance completed two successful process-route solves.
phenomenon_property: A repair notice raised for a transient, self-inflicted cause (the instance's own stop reaping its worker) must not be raised persistent, or must be withdrawable by the next healthy solve in a fresh process; a stop must not rerun the killed solve in process.
seam_rule: grep -n 'is_persistent=True' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py  (each persistent issue: is its clear path reachable from a fresh process?)

null_control.note: stop fired with no solve in flight: 0 issues raised, 0 in-process solves after stop, 0 stale after restart

reproduction_steps: setup on a real loop (rl.RealHass), wait for the first process solve
start async_run_optimization; when _read_reply is entered, await the EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP listener (_stop)
observe fallback cause 'process worker exited rc=None: Ran out of input', 1 issue is_persistent=True, 1 in-process solve after stop
restart: keep the persistent issues, clear _WORKER_FALLBACK_CAUSES and the streak; set up a new entry and solve twice
proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py: mark the stop (a module flag set by _stop) so a reply broken by our own reap is not a worker fault (no issue, no in-process rerun during stop); and/or let _clear_worker_fallback delete the issue when no entry has a latched cause in this process.
